name: Zadok
overview: Zadok was a male biblical figure identified primarily as the father of Jerusha, as recorded in 2 Kings 15:33. Beyond this familial connection, Scripture does not provide further details about his tribe or additional personal attributes. His mention serves to establish lineage in the biblical record.
namesAndTitles: The name Zadok is a proper name meaning 'righteous one.' This meaning reflects a character trait valued in the biblical context, though the name was not given directly by God. The single recorded instance of this name appears in 2 Kings 15:33.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Zadok as the father of Jerusha, as noted in 2 Kings 15:33. No other family relationships are documented for him in the biblical text, limiting our understanding of his broader family connections.
scriptureSignificance: Zadok's significance in Scripture lies chiefly in his role as the father of Jerusha, linking him to the genealogical and royal narratives of the Old Testament. This connection situates him within the broader historical and theological framework of God's providential care over His people. Although his personal story is not elaborated upon, his mention contributes to the biblical emphasis on lineage and covenantal faithfulness.
